notes.text: ECB data show the share of new house-purchase loans at a floating rate or with an initial rate fixation of up to one year rising from 7% in January 2025 to 23% in August 2026, so a growing slice of new borrowing reprices quickly with ECB policy. Household debt was 94% of GDP in 2023, mostly mortgages, and DNB notes that borrowers took on high loan-to-income levels and interest-only loan parts in the low-rate period, which amplifies the effect of rate changes on house prices.

notes.text: From January 2022 DNB imposed a minimum average risk weight on IRB banks' mortgage books, applying 12% to the part of each loan up to 55% loan to value and 45% to the remainder, or 26.85% for a loan at 100%. In April 2026 DNB decided not to extend it, so it expires on 30 November 2026, judging that housing market risks had gradually declined and that banks are less vulnerable to a price correction, with the 2% countercyclical buffer as its main resilience tool. When last extending it in 2024, DNB had cited a price-to-income index of 125 against a euro area average of 107 and an ESRB estimate of about 20% overvaluation.

notes.text: Mortgage interest remains tax deductible for owner-occupiers, but for loans taken out since 1 January 2013 only if the loan is repaid at least on an annuity or linear basis within 30 years, and for a maximum of 30 years. The rule steers new borrowing towards amortising debt, while the deduction itself continues to be capitalised into house prices.

The Affordable Rent Act (Wet betaalbare huur), in force since 1 July 2024, extended the binding points-based rent system to mid-rent homes up to 186 points, and since 1 January 2025 municipalities can act against landlords who overcharge. The cap lowers achievable rents on part of the private stock and reduces the return to buy-to-let investment in that segment.

notes.text: Nitrogen deposition rules continue to hold back permitting: in June 2026 the cabinet presented a package explicitly aimed at lifting the country off the 'nitrogen lock' (stikstofslot), and permitting in the Port of Rotterdam area is only set to resume in early 2027. DNB also cites sluggish supply as a driver of price increases, which keeps the market tight.

notes.text: The official price index of existing owner-occupied dwellings (PBK), compiled by CBS with the Kadaster, covers all registered sales of existing homes to private persons and combines Kadaster transaction data with WOZ tax valuations of the whole stock. It is monthly from January 1995, published as definitive with revisions only in exceptional cases, and excludes new-build sales.
